title: Glasgow Pub Quiz

questions.q: Which river flows through the centre of Glasgow?
Glasgow's two biggest football clubs are known together as the Old Firm. Name both.
Glasgow's Subway, with its small orange trains, is nicknamed the "Clockwork" what?
The statue of the Duke of Wellington outside the Gallery of Modern Art is famous for usually wearing what on his head?
Which Glasgow-born architect and designer drew up the Glasgow School of Art's best-known building?
Complete the city's motto: "Let Glasgow" what?
Which saint, also called Kentigern, is the patron saint of Glasgow?
In the old rhyme about Glasgow's coat of arms, there is a bird that never flew, a tree that never grew, a bell that never rang, and what that never swam?
Salvador Dalí's painting Christ of Saint John of the Cross hangs in which Glasgow museum and gallery?
Glasgow's riverside concert venue, first called the Clyde Auditorium, is now officially named after which armoured animal?

notes: River Clyde; see River Clyde Wikipedia / Glasgow City Council.
Celtic FC and Rangers FC, the 'Old Firm'; see Old Firm Wikipedia.
Clockwork Orange; origin of the nickname is disputed, so no causal claim.
Wellington statue (1844) outside GoMA, coned since the 1980s; see Duke of Wellington statue, Glasgow, Wikipedia.
Mackintosh (born Glasgow 1868) designed the Glasgow School of Art building (the Mackintosh Building); see gsa.ac.uk and Mackintosh Wikipedia.
City motto 'Let Glasgow Flourish'; see Coat of arms of Glasgow Wikipedia / Glasgow City Council.
St Mungo (Kentigern), patron saint, Glasgow Cathedral; see Saint Mungo Wikipedia.
Rhyme 'the bird that never flew, the tree that never grew, the bell that never rang, the fish that never swam'; see Glasgow City Council coat of arms page.
Dalí's Christ of Saint John of the Cross bought by Glasgow in 1952, hung at Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum; see Glasgow Museums.
Officially the SEC Armadillo since the rename.
